target: The spines of the stem segments are present (spine leaf PO:0025173, terete). 'Spineless' qualifies another organ, most likely the fruit (fruit PO:0009001 without spines, i.e. spine leaf PO:0025173 absent PATO:0000462 with context 'fruit'). Cactus spines should map to spine leaf PO:0025173, not thorn PO:0025172
fix: A bare 'spineless' inside a sentence about fruits, flowers or seeds (Cactaceae: 'fruits ... spineless', 'areoles of fruit spineless') applies to that organ only. Never record a taxon-wide spine absence from it. In Cactaceae, 'spine' maps to spine leaf PO:0025173, never thorn PO:0025172.
reason: Cylindropuntia munzii is a densely spiny cholla, and its spines are described (terete, the abaxial ones flattened). So 'spineless' must belong to another organ, probably the fruit.

target: Only the bracts of the second-order branches are absent: bract PO:0009055, absent PATO:0000462, context 'second order' (on higher order inflorescence axis PO:0009081). The main inflorescence bracts (inflorescence bract PO:0009054) are present and pale greyish green
fix: '2d order bracts absent', 'secondary bracts absent' and 'bracteoles absent' deny only the bracts of that order. Keep the order as the context and never record a generic 'bract absent'.
reason: Cyperus has leaflike inflorescence bracts. The text denies only the bracts at the second branching order.

target: The inflorescence rays are absent (higher order inflorescence axis PO:0009081 absent PATO:0000462: spikelets clustered in a sessile head). Bracts are not involved. The 'laterally whitish or dull stramineous' statement most likely describes the floral scales, not the inflorescence bracts
fix: In Cyperaceae and Apiaceae, 'rays' are the branches of the umbel or anthela: higher order inflorescence axis PO:0009081. Never map them to bract, and never to the PO 'ray' synonym (wood ray PO:0004534).
reason: 'Rays absent' means the inflorescence is a single sessile head. It says nothing about the bracts, which Cyperus gracilis has.

target: Veins absent only in the septum (septum PO:0000030; vascular bundle absent, context 'septum'). The fruit valves (fruit valve PO:0000033) have a distinct midvein. Both statements should keep their part as the location
fix: '<part> not veined', '<part> veinless' and '<part> nerveless' deny veins in that part only. Annotate the named part as the location of the absence, never a taxon-wide 'vascular bundle absent'.
reason: In Brassicaceae fruits, the septum and the valves are separate parts. One has no vein and the other has a midvein.

target: The corolla (PO:0009059) is present. What is rarely absent is the coloured ring (the yellow or purple band at the base of the corolla lobes in Dodecatheon), i.e. a colour pattern of the corolla, with frequency 'rarely'. 'Wavy ring' describes the edge of that band, not an undulate corolla
fix: In Dodecatheon/Primula, 'ring' and 'band' after a colour word are a colour zone of the corolla tube or lobe base. Annotate them as a corolla colour pattern. 'Ring absent' is never 'corolla absent', and 'wavy ring' is never 'corolla undulate'.
reason: Shooting stars always have a corolla. The ring is a coloured zone on it.

target: Axillary shoot system PO:0006343 (synonym 'axillary branch') absent on the vegetative stem. The 'branches not twisted' statement is about the inflorescence branches (higher order inflorescence axis PO:0009081). It is also a negation and should not be annotated as 'twisted'
fix: 'axillary branches absent' maps to axillary shoot system PO:0006343 absent, never 'branch absent'. 'Not twisted' and 'not <quality>' must never yield the positive quality.
reason: Dudleya rosettes do not branch from the axils, but the floral stems branch into cincinni. The two statements are about different axes.

target: Only basal (proliferous) spikelets are absent: spikelet PO:0009051, absent, context 'basal'. The single terminal spikelet is present and acute
fix: 'basal spikelets absent' and 'proliferous spikelets absent' (Eleocharis) deny only the extra spikelets at the culm base. Keep 'basal' as the context and never record 'spikelet absent'.
reason: Every Eleocharis has a terminal spikelet. Basal spikelets are an optional extra kind.

target: The caudex is absent (a woody perennial stem base; no PO class, so stem PO:0009047 with context 'caudex', or a FLOPO anatomy class). The aerial stems are present and solid
fix: PO lists 'caudex' as a synonym of stem PO:0009047. 'caudex absent' and 'without a caudex' must never become 'stem absent'. Keep 'caudex' as the context, or map it to a dedicated caudex class.
reason: A plant without a caudex still has stems. The error comes from the synonym in the lexicon.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent only immediately below the involucre (position context 'immediately below involucre', involucre PO:0009100). Leaflike bracts are present at the inflorescence nodes
fix: 'bracts absent immediately below <part>', 'bracts absent at/near <part>' and 'ebracteate below <part>' give a position. Keep the position as the context and never record 'bract absent' for the taxon.

target: Peduncle (PO:0009053) present only in the fork of the proximal node and absent elsewhere. Context 'except in fork of proximal node'. The villous statement describes those peduncles
fix: '<part> absent except <position>' means the part is present at that position. Record presence with the position as the context, never a plain absence.
reason: The sentence itself says peduncles occur at one position, and those are the ones described as villous.

target: The nectary on the leaf is present (extrafloral nectary PO:0009057 on the abaxial base of the leaf midvein PO:0020139). The nectaries that are absent are those of another member, most likely the calyx or involucel (context 'calyx'/'sepal')
fix: In Malvaceae (Hibiscus, Gossypium), 'nectaries absent' inside the calyx, bractlet or involucel sentence refers to that organ. Keep the organ as the context. Leaf-midvein nectaries map to extrafloral nectary PO:0009057.
reason: Hibiscus descriptions treat leaf nectaries and calyx nectaries separately. One can be present and the other absent.

target: The shoots lack annual constrictions: shoot axis PO:0025029 (or stem PO:0009047) without zones of shorter leaves marking each year's growth. The whole plant is present, and the juvenile growth is erect
fix: 'annual constrictions absent' / 'present' (Huperzia, Lycopodiaceae) describe the pattern of leaf length along the shoot. Annotate the shoot axis with that context, and never let a missing head noun fall back to whole plant PO:0000003.
reason: The phrase is a growth-pattern character of the shoots. The whole plant cannot be absent.

target: Bracts (PO:0009055) absent only on the peduncle (location peduncle PO:0009053). The involucral bracts (phyllaries, involucral bract PO:0009045) are present and glabrous or hirsute; that statement should go to involucral bract
fix: '<axis> ebracteate' (peduncles, scapes, stems ebracteate) means there are no bracts along that axis. Keep the axis as the location. It never extends to the involucral bracts/phyllaries of Asteraceae.
reason: Leontodon heads always have phyllaries. Only the peduncle is bractless.

target: Cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent (PATO:0000462). The basal leaves are present and sessile or narrowed to a petiole
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' maps to cauline leaf PO:0000013, and 'basal leaves absent' to rosette leaf PO:0000014. Neither ever falls back to leaf PO:0025034.
reason: Lewisia has a basal rosette. Only the stem leaves are denied.

target: 'Without anthers' defines the staminodes (staminode PO:0009077, the outer petaloid stamens of Mentzelia). The fertile stamens have anthers. 'Epidermis smooth' is a seed character (seed coat PO:0009088 smooth), wrongly assigned to anther
fix: '<outer/petaloid> stamens ... without anthers' and 'sterile stamens without anthers' map to staminode PO:0009077, never 'anther absent'. A trait whose head noun is 'epidermis' or 'seed coat' after a seed sentence belongs to the seed.
reason: Mentzelia has outer staminodes without anthers among fertile stamens. Smooth epidermis is described for the seeds.

target: Only the recurved flap of the seed coat over the hilum is absent (seed coat PO:0009088 with context 'flap over hilum', hilum PO:0020063). The seed is present and tuberculate
fix: '<feature> over/at/on <part> absent' denies the feature, not the part it sits on or the organ that carries it. Keep the feature as the absent entity, with the part as the location.
reason: The flap is a small structure of the seed coat in Mentzelia sect. Trachyphytum. The seed itself is described.

target: Petiole (PO:0020038) absent on the distal leaves, present or absent on the proximal leaves. Context 'distal leaves' versus 'proximal leaves'
fix: A parenthesis '(distal leaves)', '(proximal leaves)' or '(cauline leaves)' after a value restricts it to those leaves. Keep it as the context.
reason: The leaves along the stem differ: the upper ones are sessile and the lower ones may be petiolate.

target: Nothing is absent. The bracts (PO:0009055) are present and ovate, and they do not conceal the capsule (capsule fruit PO:0030091). At most, record a relation 'not concealing capsule'; otherwise drop it
fix: 'not concealing <part>', 'not covering <part>' and 'not exceeding <part>' are negated relations between two present parts. They are never an absence of either part.
reason: The phrase compares bract size with the capsule. It does not deny the bracts.

target: Petals (PO:0009032) variably absent or present (the name 'subapetala'). When present, they are clawed. Context: frequency 'often/sometimes absent'
fix: 'petals absent or present', 'petals 0-5' and 'petals often absent' record a variable presence. Keep the frequency, and annotate the other petal qualities as applying 'when present'.
reason: Micranthes subapetala is named for its often reduced or missing petals. Plants with petals have clawed ones.

target: Bracts absent only on the scape/peduncle (bract PO:0009055, location peduncle PO:0009053). The involucral bracts (PO:0009045) are present with acute apices
fix: A bare 'ebracteate' in an Asteraceae description belongs to the scape or peduncle sentence. Keep that axis as the location and never deny the involucral bracts.

target: Only the axillary leaf fascicles are absent (leaves on short axillary shoots: axillary shoot system PO:0006343 absent, or leaf PO:0025034 with context 'axillary'). The main leaves are present and flexuous

target: Only overwintering stems are absent (stem PO:0009047, context 'wintering'; an annual habit). The flowering stems are present and glabrous or stipitate-glandular
fix: '<kind> stems absent' (wintering, sterile, trailing, prostrate, flowering) denies that kind of stem only. Keep the kind as the context, and never record 'stem absent'.

target: Stems (PO:0009047) are present and ascending to erect. There are no trailing stems, so this is a habit statement, not an absence

target: Bracts absent on the flowering stems/peduncles (bract PO:0009055, location peduncle PO:0009053). The involucral bracts (PO:0009045) are present with glabrous faces; that statement belongs to involucral bract
fix: 'Stems (peduncles) ebracteate' and '<axis> ebracteate' locate the absence on the axis. Never deny the phyllaries, and map 'faces glabrous' in the phyllary sentence to involucral bract PO:0009045.

target: Short hairs absent on the leaflets: trichome PO:0000282, absent, context 'short', location leaflet PO:0020049. The leaflets are present with revolute margins

target: Short hairs (trichome PO:0000282, context 'short') absent on the petiole (PO:0020038). The 'soft' statement most likely describes the long hairs of the petiole, not the petiole itself
fix: '<kind> hairs absent' denies that kind of trichome on the part in the sentence. A texture word (soft, stiff, crisped) next to a hair word in a vestiture list applies to the hairs.

target: Only leaflike bracts subtending the heads are absent (bract PO:0009055, context 'leaflike, subtending head'). The involucral bracts (phyllaries, PO:0009045) are present and obtuse; that statement belongs to involucral bract

target: Stipules (PO:0020041) are present but caducous, i.e. not persistent around the buds. Neither an absence nor 'non-deciduous' is supported. Drop both, or record stipule 'not persistent (at bud)'

target: Basal (rosette) leaves absent: rosette leaf PO:0000014 absent (PATO:0000462). The cauline leaves (PO:0000013), including the submerged dissected ones, are present

target: Only the tubercles (calli) on the inner tepals/valves are absent (tepal PO:0009033 with context 'tubercle/callus'). Do not use tubercle PO:0025352, which is the cactus podarium. The tepals are present, with obtuse apices. Rumex perianth parts map to tepal PO:0009033 rather than sepal
